title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: SGR personnel
tiers.description: All directors, officers, employees, contractors and consultants (including fixed term/task contractors and employees of incorporated contractors/consultants) of SGR, its subsidiaries and associate companies. Those who are not Designated Persons may trade in SGR securities at any time, provided they have no inside information and comply with confidentiality obligations.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All executive and non-executive Directors of SGR or its subsidiaries; independent Compliance Committee members; Executives reporting to the MD&CEO and their Direct Reports; the Executive team and their Direct Reports; executive assistants of Directors/Executives; financial reporting team members; and other individuals designated by the Board, Chair, MD&CEO or Company Secretary. Subject to Blackout Periods and a universal clearance-to-trade requirement.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: the Chair of the Audit Committee provides clearance.

tiers.name: Other Directors (including Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer)
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: the Chair provides clearance.

tiers.name: Executives, Executive Direct Reports, executive assistants, financial reporting team members and other designated persons
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: any one of the Company Secretary, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, or Chief Financial Officer provides clearance.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse, de-facto partner, dependent children, family trusts, family companies, self-managed or other superannuation funds and entities controlled by a Designated Person, or any person or entity that might reasonably be associated with them (for example, joint venture partners or their employees or contractors).

definitions.hedging_definition: any hedging arrangement, financial instrument or derivative relating to SGR ordinary shares (for example, warrants, exchange-traded and over-the-counter options, and contracts for difference (CFD))

commencement of trading on the first trading day after SGR releases its quarterly report (ASX Appendix 4C) for the March quarter
commencement of trading on the first trading day SGR releases its quarterly report (ASX Appendix 4C) for the September quarter

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, the Chair, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, or the Company Secretary may determine any other Blackout Period from time to time. Confidentiality of such a determination is not addressed.

rules.detail: SGR securities expressly include 'any hedging arrangement, financial instrument or derivative relating to SGR ordinary shares', naming warrants, exchange-traded and OTC options and CFDs, with no venue limit. Designated Persons must obtain clearance to trade in SGR securities at any time. However, a derivative structured so that its settlement 'may lead to the ownership and rights of the securities being transferred to a third party' is separately barred by section 17.
rules.evidence: any hedging arrangement, financial instrument or derivative relating to SGR ordinary shares (for example, warrants, exchange-traded and over-the-counter options, and contracts for difference (CFD))

rules.detail: SGR personnel who are not Designated Persons may trade in SGR securities (including the derivatives named in section 3) at any time, provided they have no inside information and comply with confidentiality obligations; no clearance is required.
rules.evidence: All employees, contractors and their Associates who are not Designated Persons may trade in SGR securities at any time, provided they do not have inside information and otherwise comply with their obligations of confidentiality.

rules.detail: Any incentive-plan participant (Designated Person or not) is banned from hedging unvested performance rights or options, with forfeiture of the relevant securities as the sanction for breach.
rules.evidence: If you participate in any of SGR's employee or executive incentive plans you are prohibited from hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance rights or options and you must not enter into any derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance rights or options granted under such plans.

rules.detail: The same ban extends to 'restricted shares' (vested shares still subject to a holding restriction under the incentive plan); breach results in forfeiture.
rules.evidence: you are prohibited from hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance rights or options ... Breaches of this prohibition will result in the relevant shares, performance rights or options being forfeited by you.

rules.detail: The section 19 hedging ban is confined to restricted shares and unvested plan rights/options; once shares vest and any holding restriction lifts, hedging (a named SGR security) is not separately banned and instead requires ordinary clearance under section 8, subject to the Corporate Reputation Test and section 17's ban on any transfer-triggering financial arrangement.
rules.evidence: you must obtain clearance to trade before you or any of your Associates engage in trading of SGR securities at any time.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a forward sale, prepaid forward or similar structure is a 'financial arrangement involving SGR securities which may lead to the ownership and rights of the securities being transferred to a third party', which section 17 bans outright.
rules.evidence: You must not enter into any financial arrangements involving SGR securities which may lead to the ownership and rights of the securities being transferred to a third party.

rules.detail: Unconditional ban on short selling, expressed as applying to 'you' (SGR personnel generally, not only Designated Persons), with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from engaging in short selling of SGR securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are expressly named as an SGR security; Designated Persons need clearance to trade, and a CFD structured to transfer ownership/rights to a third party would separately be barred by section 17.
rules.evidence: any hedging arrangement, financial instrument or derivative relating to SGR ordinary shares (for example, warrants, exchange-traded and over-the-counter options, and contracts for difference (CFD))

rules.detail: Absolute ban on margin loans involving SGR securities for Designated Persons and their Associates, with no clearance route referenced.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are prohibited from entering into margin loans or other financing arrangements involving SGR securities or in relation to which SGR securities may be used as security of any type against loan repayments.

rules.detail: SGR securities may not be used as security of any type against loan repayments by Designated Persons or their Associates, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are prohibited from entering into margin loans or other financing arrangements involving SGR securities or in relation to which SGR securities may be used as security of any type against loan repayments.

rules.detail: Blanket, unconditional ban covering margin loans and 'other financing arrangements' involving SGR securities, plus any arrangement using them as security, for Designated Persons and their Associates; no tier, vesting-state or clearance carve-out.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates are prohibited from entering into margin loans or other financing arrangements involving SGR securities or in relation to which SGR securities may be used as security of any type against loan repayments.

rules.detail: Clearance to trade within 12 months of acquisition will generally not be granted, and will only be granted in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a court order) where the trade is the only reasonable course of action. Disposals shortly after exercise/vesting under an incentive plan are not treated as short-term trading.
rules.evidence: Clearance to trade will generally not be granted for proposed trades that are within 12 months of acquisition.

carve_outs: trading of SGR ordinary shares shortly after their acquisition following the exercise or vesting of options or rights pursuant to SGR's employee or executive incentive plans (or other equity-based remuneration schemes)
short_term.evidence: Clearance to trade will generally not be granted for proposed trades that are within 12 months of acquisition.

exceptions.evidence: an offer concerning SGR securities made to all or most of the securityholders (for example a bonus issue, security purchase plan, rights issue or equal access buy-back)
a disposal of rights or entitlements acquired under a renounceable pro-rata issue
an acquisition of securities under a pro-rata issue

an acquisition of SGR securities under a security purchase plan or a dividend reinvestment plan that is available to all eligible holders of securities of the same class, where the participation in the plan was not commenced or amended during a Blackout Period

an allocation of, or agreement to acquire, or vesting of SGR securities under an employee or executive incentive plan (however, the prohibitions in this policy will apply to any subsequent disposal of SGR securities acquired under those employee or executive incentive plans)
elections to participate in a corporate action involving SGR (including undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, an announced takeover offer)
a disposal of SGR securities as part of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

a transfer of SGR securities resulting in no change in the underlying beneficial interest (for example, transfer from one personal shareholding to another personal shareholding or into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the individual is a beneficiary), where the initial acquisition of those securities has previously been approved in accordance with this policy
investments by a fund or other scheme (such as an independent superannuation fund) where the investment decision is at the discretion of a third party
cancellation of SGR securities as a result of failure to vest or other forfeiture of securities received as part of performance based remuneration

vesting (but not any subsequent sale) of SGR securities as a result of meeting performance hurdles or release of the securities from holding lock, in respect of securities received as part of performance based remuneration

where a Designated Person is a trustee, trading in SGR securities by that trust provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Blackout Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that hold SGR securities as part of its portfolio

exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship such as a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant securities

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: A separate Minimum Shareholding Policy is referenced as related information but this Securities Trading Policy does not address whether hedged or encumbered shares count towards it.

external_documents: SGR's employee or executive incentive plan terms and conditions
exemption_authority: The Chair, the Chair of the Audit Committee, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer or the Company Secretary (as applicable to the applicant) determine on a case-by-case basis whether exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a court order, without limitation) justify clearance during a Blackout Period or within 12 months of acquisition, only where the trade is the only reasonable course of action; clearance may be refused without reasons and the decision is final.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons and their Associates are prohibited from entering into margin loans or other financing arrangements involving SGR securities or in relation to which SGR securities may be used as security of any type against loan repayments.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is banned outright for Designated Persons and their Associates, with no clearance mechanism anywhere in the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not enter into any financial arrangements involving SGR securities which may lead to the ownership and rights of the securities being transferred to a third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This standalone sentence (not limited to financing) would also catch a physically-settled call, forward, or other monetisation structure under which the bank could ultimately take the shares, closing off even an unfunded, physically-settled collar structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If prior written clearance for a proposed trade is required to be obtained under this policy, the clearance will not be granted if the proposed trade would not satisfy the Corporate Reputation Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically permitted collar over vested, unrestricted shares can be refused clearance on a subjective perception-based test (how the trade would look if reported in the media).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance to trade: ... will remain in force for 3 business days from and including the date it is given ... [section 13] Any trading that is the subject of prior written clearance must be executed within five business days from and including the date the written clearance is granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy states two different execution deadlines (3 vs 5 business days) for the same clearance, creating timing uncertainty for scheduling collar execution that should be clarified with the Company Secretary before relying on either figure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you are prohibited from hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance rights or options ... Breaches of this prohibition will result in the relevant shares, performance rights or options being forfeited by you.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary disciplinary consequences, breaching the hedging ban on unvested/restricted incentive securities results in forfeiture of those securities themselves, a severe additional risk if a collar were mistakenly written over still-restricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: SGR will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through an associate, trust or offshore counterparty to avoid the section 17 financing ban or section 19 hedging ban is unlikely to succeed given this express substance-over-form mandate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any person or entity that might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with the Designated Person (for example, joint venture partners or their employees or contractors)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Associates net is unusually broad, extending beyond family and controlled entities to any 'reasonably associated' person, making it harder to structure the collar counterparty relationship around the restriction.

summary: A funded collar is not available for a Designated Person (which includes all directors and executives) under this policy. Section 17 bans, without any clearance route, margin loans or other financing arrangements involving SGR securities and any use of SGR securities as security, so the loan leg is prohibited outright for the executive and their Associates; a separate sentence in section 17 also bars any financial arrangement that could lead to the shares' ownership or rights transferring to a third party, which would catch a physically-settled put or call as well. Hedging of restricted shares and unvested performance rights or options is banned outright with forfeiture as the sanction, but once shares vest and any holding restriction lifts, hedging is not separately prohibited and could proceed with ordinary written clearance under section 8, subject to Blackout Periods, the 12-month short-term trading presumption, and the subjective Corporate Reputation Test. Short selling is banned outright with no exceptions. Given the section 17 financing and anti-transfer bans have no exemption authority or carve-out, the funded collar structure as a whole is blocked, though a cash-settled, unfunded hedge over vested unrestricted shares might be clearable on a case-by-case basis.
